text: {"findings":[{"type":"UNSUPPORTED_CLAIM","title":"35% contact reduction stated as fact without a source","detail":"The 35% reduction in where-is-my-order contacts has no cited source or analysis. It also conflicts with the proposal's own target of 8.4 to 7.0 per 100, which is about a 17% reduction.","evidence_quote":"This will cut where-is-my-order contacts by 35%.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Cite the source for the 35% figure (prior test, benchmark, or analysis) or remove it. Reconcile it with the 7.0 per 100 target."},{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"Live tracking involves location data with no privacy review recorded","detail":"Live tracking push notifications share real-time driver location and use customer notification and location data, which is personal data. The Reviews section records only team capacity, with no privacy or legal review.","evidence_quote":"Notification platform team has capacity.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Record privacy/data-protection review of the live tracking and notification data use, including driver location sharing and customer notification consent, before launch."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"No guardrails for notification side effects","detail":"A new push notification changes customer-facing messaging behavior, but the only guardrail is Delivery CSAT. Notification opt-out or disable rate and delivery or ETA-accuracy side effects are not covered. Inaccurate 5-minute alerts could also increase contacts.","evidence_quote":"Delivery CSAT: stop if it falls by more than 0.05.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails such as push opt-out/disable rate, notification accuracy (alert sent vs. actual arrival time), and on-time delivery rate, each with stop thresholds."}]}
